correctness.rationale: Independent row and column translations change only phases; applying L and its inverse transpose preserves pairings. The two row orbits follow from affine transitivity on triangles and the complements of pairs on a five-point line. For the line orbit, distinct first coordinates are necessary and sufficient by Vandermonde; the two pentagonal triple types contribute five projections each and 125 lifts per projection. I independently enumerated all 4,600 representative minors using det(M M*) rather than the supplied determinant expansion: with cyclic off-diagonal Gram entries a,b,c, det(M M*)=27-3(|a|²+|b|²+|c|²)+2 Re(abc). Exact reduction of integer character sums gave the stated spectra, the 625 first-coordinate maximizing lifts and exactly the disjoint union of the two displayed 25-element cap orbits. Counting 300 line triples and 2,000 triangles gives 287,500 maximizing, 615,000 singular and 4,675,000 nonsingular support pairs. Consistent with the explicit 2,300-choice quantifier, each support has three distinct points and the two supports may coincide.
residual_risks: Unnormalized character matrix, exactly F_5^2 and exactly order-three minors; determinant magnitude does not classify the condition number.

value.rationale: This is the full volume distribution of the natural three-point Fourier basis-selection problem in characteristic five. In particular it gives the exact geometric cost of constraining the row support to a line (a loss of five in the best squared volume) and all the attainable optimal frequency supports. Neither the known rank counts nor a computation of one maximizing example answers those design questions.
residual_risks: No inference about condition numbers or general primes.
